title: ReadableStream & TransformStream: BYOB Buffer Zero-Copy Piping

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Normally, reading a stream is like a water fountain that pours water into new paper cups over and over, throwing each cup away. A 'BYOB' (Bring Your Own Buffer) stream lets you bring your own durable thermos: the fountain pours directly into your thermos with zero wasted cups and zero extra copying.
progressiveExplaining.junior: Bun natively implements the WHATWG Web Streams API: `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, and `TransformStream`. You can consume streams using `for await (const chunk of stream)`, pipe streams with `stream.pipeThrough(transform).pipeTo(dest)`, and use BYOB ('Bring Your Own Buffer') readers (`stream.getReader({ mode: 'byob' })`) to read raw binary data into pre-allocated `Uint8Array` buffers with zero garbage collection overhead.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Bun's Web Streams implementation is written in native Zig, binding Web Streams directly to operating system file descriptors and TCP sockets. In Node.js, Web Streams were historically implemented as a JavaScript compatibility wrapper over legacy `EventEmitter` streams (`node:stream`), adding allocation overhead. Bun's native implementation supports BYOB readers to read kernel bytes directly into user-allocated memory pages.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When calling `reader.read(new Uint8Array(buffer))`, Bun passes the raw memory address of the TypedArray's backing store directly to the underlying `read(2)` / `recv(2)` syscall. This eliminates intermediate chunk buffer allocations in the JavaScriptCore heap, maximizing L1/L2 CPU cache utilization during high-speed data transcoding.

interviewGotchas.question: What does BYOB stand for in the Web Streams standard, and why does it improve performance?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of low-level memory allocation in streams.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: BYOB stands for **'Bring Your Own Buffer'**. In standard streams (`reader.read()`), the stream engine allocates a *new* `Uint8Array` chunk on every single read, creating garbage collection pressure. With BYOB (`stream.getReader({ mode: 'byob' })`), the consumer passes an *existing* `Uint8Array` to `reader.read(buffer)`. The runtime reads bytes directly into that pre-allocated memory, eliminating all per-chunk memory allocations.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: A stream must be a byte stream (backed by a byte source) to support `mode: 'byob'`; calling it on an object stream throws a `TypeError`.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you pipe a Web Stream into an HTTP response in Bun?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of response stream piping in Bun servers.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Simply pass the `ReadableStream` directly into the `Response` constructor: `return new Response(myReadableStream)`. Bun handles backpressure, chunk encoding, and socket closing automatically.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not buffer the stream with `await stream.text()` before creating the response; pass the stream itself.
